messages:
maya: Thanks for the runtime roadmap segment. A few follow-ups from product and customer success.
maya: 1) Per-route QoS: can we set priority weights so some routes always get smaller batches to hit low-latency SLOs?
taylor: Yes. We're adding per-route qos_weight + latency_target fields. Runtime will bias batch formation to respect weights at the cost of throughput.
alex: Implementation: a lightweight shaping layer that tags requests and enforces a max_hold_time per-priority. Default max_hold_time=8ms for high-pri routes.
rami: 2) Kernel telemetry: customers want visibility into which kernel variant served a given request for debugging and billing.
jin: We'll add kernel_variant to trace logs and export it to the console traces. High-cardinality -> sampled at 2% by default for hosted.
ops-bot: [info] Enabling kernel_variant export increases trace storage; Dedicated customers can opt-in at higher sampling.
maya: 3) Autoscaler decisions: when autoscaler reduces batch sizes under load, how do we avoid oscillation?
taylor: Autoscaler uses dampening windows and looks at sliding p99 over 30s. We also include a cooldown of 60s after a scale decision.
alex: Also we now smooth decisions using per-route batch-size histograms so transient spikes don't flip policies.
maya: 4) Can we set strict kernel pinning without fallbacks? Some customers want deterministic behavior for regulatory reasons.
taylor: Yes, kernel_policy.allow_fallback=false will enforce strict pinning. Warning: this increases risk of capacity-induced errors; we surface simulation checks before commit.
rami: 5) Observability: will the console show batch composition and KV hit/miss rates per-route?
jin: Console will add a batch-composition view and per-route kv_hit_rate metric. Both are time-series and can be filtered by model, region, and route.
maya: Action items: taylor to post RFC for per-route QoS and kernel pinning. jin to add console mockups. alex to write a short note on max_hold_time tradeoffs.
taylor: I'll publish RFC early next week and tag this thread.
maya: Awesome, thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
